questions.stem: What is the purpose of a database index?
options: To enforce foreign key relationships
To compress table data on disk
To store a backup copy of the table
To partition the table across nodes
To enhance the performance of database queries on tables
questions.explanation: An index is used to enhance the performance of database queries on tables by holding the information needed to reach data quickly.

questions.stem: What happens if a table has more indexes than it needs?
options: Query performance always improves further
Performance can decrease
The table becomes read-only
The primary key is dropped
Nothing changes, because unused indexes are ignored
questions.explanation: Although many indexes can be created, having more than required can decrease performance as well.

questions.stem: When is an index normally created on a table?
options: Before any data has been loaded
Only when the table is archived
Only after a backup has been taken
When the database starts growing
Only when the table is partitioned
questions.explanation: Indexes are normally created once the database starts growing and lookups become expensive.

questions.stem: In the Library of Congress analogy for indexing, roughly how many items does the library hold?
options: About 170 million
About 17 million
About 1.7 billion
About 70 million
About 700 thousand
questions.explanation: The Library of Congress, described as the largest library in the world, houses approximately 170 million items.

questions.stem: What does the Library of Congress analogy illustrate about why indexes are needed?
options: That libraries need more staff than databases
That every book must be stored in alphabetical order
That an index contains all the information needed to access items quickly and efficiently, just as a database index does for data
That searching manually is faster than searching by computer
That large collections should be split across buildings
questions.explanation: Asking for the library's index of names and locations is the smart way to find a book in ten minutes; a database index plays the same role for data.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of indexing?
options: It speeds up INSERT and UPDATE statements
It removes the need for a primary key
It allows the table to be partitioned freely
It reduces the total number of I/O operations needed to retrieve data
It stores the ROWID in every index entry
questions.explanation: Indexing reduces the number of I/O operations needed to retrieve data and offers faster search and retrieval.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of indexing?
options: It decreases performance in INSERT, DELETE and UPDATE queries
It increases the number of I/O operations for reads
It makes data retrieval slower for users
It increases tablespace by storing every row twice
It prevents the creation of a primary key
questions.explanation: SQL indexing decreases the performance of INSERT, DELETE and UPDATE queries, since the index must be maintained.

questions.stem: What does a database management system need on a table in order to perform indexing?
options: A foreign key to another table
At least one partition
A primary key with a unique value
A clustered and a non-clustered index already in place
A column store
questions.explanation: To perform indexing, the database management system needs a primary key on the table with a unique value.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed among the types of index?
options: B-Tree Index
Bitmap Index
Hash Index
Reverse Index
Quadtree Index
questions.explanation: B-Tree, Bitmap, Hash and Reverse indexes are all listed, alongside many others; a Quadtree index is not.

questions.stem: Which restriction applies to an index-organised table?
options: It cannot have a primary key
It is not allowed to be partitioned
It cannot be queried with SQL
It must use a bitmap index
It cannot be backed up
questions.explanation: Among the disadvantages of indexing is that you are not allowed to partition an index-organised table.
